title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Our continuous batching pipeline currently aggregates requests with a loose time-based policy which can cause significant padding waste when sequence length distribution is heavy-tailed. For customer workloads with mixed short and long prompts (chat + embeddings warmups), padding increases per-token compute and pushes more requests to slower kernels. This PR introduces sequence-length bucketing and a padding-minimizing batch allocator to reduce wasted tokens and improve p50/p95 latency for common workloads.

Approach: Implement lightweight seqlen bucketing at the request-routing layer and extend the batch allocator to prefer batching requests with similar effective sequence lengths. The change is intentionally heuristic-driven and runtime-configurable: buckets are defined by percentiles from an adaptive sampler, and the allocator uses a best-fit padding minimization objective with a small lookahead window to avoid starvation. Kernels now receive a batch metadata tag with the expected padding ratio so the kernel selector can prefer kernels that perform better for the batch shape (e.g. dense vs. patched attention kernels).

Heuristics and config: Default bucket boundaries are computed from a 1k-sample sliding window with stable fallbacks for low-volume tails. Config knobs added (runtime/scheduler/heuristics.py): bucket_percentiles, max_padding_ratio, lookahead_batch_size, and seqlen_bucket_ttl. Production defaults were chosen to balance latency improvements with fairness. Buckets are coarse (4-6) to keep scheduling overhead low.

KV cache and kernels: Because bucketing groups similar sequence lengths, we reduce KV-cache fragmentation across devices. We also added an optional "kv-retain" hint for batches where many requests are expected to continue (chat sessions) to avoid premature evictions. On the kernel side we pass batch_shape hints to the kernel selector so that kernels with better packed attention paths are preferred for low-padding batches. The implementation is backward-compatible: if the runtime config disables bucketing, behavior falls back to the previous continuous-batching policy.

Benchmarks & results: Microbenchmarks ran on our perf-canary cluster (A100x8). On mixed chat workloads (short: 8-20 tokens, long: 256-1024 tokens) we observe: median token latency -5% overall, p95 latency -12% for tail-heavy requests, throughput +18% tokens/s, and compute cost per token -11%. For predominantly short request workloads we see up to 25% improvement in effective GPU utilization. Detailed benchmark harness and sample traces are under benchmarks/dynamic_batching/.

Testing: Added unit tests for the bucket calculator and allocator (tests/batching/test_seqlen_buckets.py), integration tests across scheduler<->kernel selection boundary, and end-to-end perf tests on the perf-canary job. CI includes a perf-benchmark job that compares this branch to main on synthetic traces.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind a runtime flag (scheduler.enable_seqlen_bucketing). Rollout will be staged: 1) enable on a small canary pool for 48h with increased tracing; 2) expand to 10% of serving capacity and monitor p50/p95, KV-cache evictions, and request fairness; 3) full roll if no regressions. Alerting added to the console for padding ratio regressions and unexpected KV eviction spikes.

Backward compatibility and docs: No API surface changes. Added configuration docs and operational guidance at benchmarks/dynamic_batching/README.md and redwood-docs/runtime/continuous-batching.md.

Notes: This change reduces padding waste but does add a small scheduling overhead; we measured median scheduler CPU increase of ~2-3% which is acceptable given GPU improvements. Future follow-ups: dynamic bucket count tuning, cross-queue coalescing, and tighter kernel selection heuristics for quantized models.

release_notes: Reduced padding waste by bucketing requests by sequence length and adding a padding-minimizing batch allocator. Improves throughput and tail latency for mixed-length workloads. Feature gated behind scheduler.enable_seqlen_bucketing. See redwood-docs/runtime/continuous-batching.md for operational guidance.
